attacks.claim: The public launch post, sent to all publishers at 16:00 UTC, says Smart Send is live for every publication and that issues arrive up to 5× faster. That contradicts the 5%/25%/100% cohort ramp meant to gate the default, and a sent announcement cannot be recalled by flipping a flag.
attacks.evidence: "Smart Send Time is live for every publication today" vs "ramp SMART_SEND_DEFAULT by publication cohort: 5% (week 1), 25% (week 2), 100% (week 3)"

attacks.claim: The production config sets Smart Send to default-on for all publications on day one, so the staged ramp described in the plan does not match what the deploy does.
attacks.evidence: "SMART_SEND_DEFAULT=on" in deploy/prod/send-worker.env vs "ramp SMART_SEND_DEFAULT by publication cohort: 5% (week 1), 25% (week 2), 100% (week 3)"

attacks.claim: On any whole-batch SES error, every recipient in the batch is recorded as a failure and excluded from the rest of the issue, with no retry. A transient throttle or 5xx therefore silently drops up to 50 subscribers per batch and reports them as 'Not delivered'.
attacks.evidence: "if err != nil { for _, r := range batch.Recipients { failures.Record(ctx, batch.IssueID, r.SubscriberID, errCode(err)) } ... continue }" and "those recipients are excluded from the issue's remaining sends"

attacks.claim: Default-on Smart Send holds time-sensitive issues (breaking news, election results, weather alerts) up to 18 hours for roughly 40% of publications. The artifact does not segment or exempt them, which defeats the core purpose of those sends.
attacks.evidence: "Issues are held for at most 18 hours. Enabled by default for all publications" vs "4,480 of them (40%) are news or local-news outlets whose issues are time-sensitive (breaking news, election results, weather alerts)"

attacks.claim: The throughput QA ran with SES throttling simulated off, and the only real-SES signal showed throttling on 4 workers. The sub-3-minute goal and production behaviour under real SES limits are therefore unobserved.
attacks.evidence: "4 workers were throttled intermittently, so QA ran with SES throttling simulated off via the sandbox mock" and "50k-recipient issue end to end | 4 workers, batch 50 | Pass, 0 failures, 11 min"

attacks.claim: Production runs 48 workers, each measured at about 25 msg/s in a single-worker run, against a stated 300 msg/s SES ceiling. The config is not reconciled with the quota, and the bottleneck is not identified, so throttling into the failure path is plausible.
attacks.evidence: "SEND_WORKERS=48" with "~25 msg/s sustained" per worker and "SES production account limits (us-east-1): 300 messages/second"

attacks.claim: The '5× faster' claim in the public launch post is not supported. The measured result is 11 minutes for 50k, with throttling off, and the 3-minute goal is unmeasured. The implied ratio is not 5× under any measured run.
attacks.evidence: "every Inkwell issue reaches inboxes up to 5× faster" vs "cut median time-to-inbox for a 50k-subscriber issue from 14 min to under 3 min" and "Pass, 0 failures, 11 min"

attacks.claim: The 71% within ±1h Smart Send accuracy has no naive baseline such as a fixed-hour send, and it covers 2,000 sampled subscribers. The 3% open-rate lift gate therefore has no stated prior or measured basis.
attacks.evidence: "predicted hour within ±1h of actual top open hour, 2,000 sampled subscribers | — | 71%" and "open-rate lift ≥ 3% vs control"

attacks.claim: The batch is acked after the SES call with no idempotency key or dedupe. A crash or redelivery after SES accepted the batch could double-send to subscribers.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: idempotency key or dedupe on SendBulkEmail; "q.Ack(ctx, batch)" follows the send

attacks.claim: The pager covers only queue lag and complaint rate. send.batch_failed and the growth of send_failures records have no alarm, so silent recipient loss would not page on-call. The complaint thresholds also disagree: dashboards alarm at 0.08% and the pager fires at 0.1%.
attacks.evidence: "On-call pager: queue lag > 10 min, complaint rate > 0.1%." with "send.batch_failed" listed only under Dashboards, vs "alarms at 4% / 0.08%"

attacks.claim: The pipeline cuts over to 100% of sends at deploy with no canary, and the Sidekiq rollback's sub-2-minute drain is not shown to have been tested under load. The public launch is set for the same day with no burn-in window.
attacks.evidence: "deploy Monday 09:00 UTC to 100% of sends" and "in-flight batches drain in < 2 min" with ABSENT: rollback exercise in QA table, and "Launch post: Mon 2026-11-09 16:00 UTC"

attacks.claim: Default-on delay of commercial email by up to 18 hours, with no per-recipient opt-out, notice, or consent step, is a material change to delivery timing. No legal or ToS review of this change is documented, including for time-bound election and weather content.
attacks.evidence: "Enabled by default for all publications; publishers can turn it off in Settings → Delivery" with ABSENT: compliance or legal review of Smart Send holds

attacks.claim: Per-subscriber open-hour profiles are derived from 90 days of opens and used to hold sends. No retention period, consent basis, subscriber disclosure, or publisher access control is stated.
attacks.evidence: "predicts each subscriber's most likely open hour from their last 90 days of opens" with ABSENT: retention, consent, and access controls

attacks.claim: Per-recipient results are matched to batch.Recipients by index with no length or ordering check, so a short or reordered SES response could misattribute failures to the wrong subscribers.
attacks.evidence: "for i, res := range out.BulkEmailEntryResults { ... batch.Recipients[i].SubscriberID"

attacks.claim: The shared 300 msg/s and 25M/day quota has no per-publication fairness or backpressure, so one large issue can crowd out others.
attacks.evidence: "SES production account limits (us-east-1): 300 messages/second, 25M/day" with no fairness mechanism described

attacks.claim: The top Q3 customer request was time-zone scheduled sends, which already shipped. Smart Send is a different feature that removes publisher control of send time by default and does not address that request.
attacks.evidence: "Top customer request in Q3: scheduled sends with time zone support (shipped in 2026.08)."

attacks.claim: Rollback releases only held issues. Issues already delivered at a delayed hour cannot be recalled.
attacks.evidence: "held issues are released immediately"

attacks.claim: The 'Not delivered' report does not distinguish retryable throttle losses from permanent subscriber-side failures, so publishers may misread the cause.
attacks.evidence: "shown to publishers in the issue report under 'Not delivered'"

attacks.claim: The launch copy 'Nothing to set up; it's already on' hides the delay trade-off and the opt-out location from publishers.
attacks.evidence: "Nothing to set up; it's already on."

attacks.claim: Throttle-driven retries would consume SES quota and spend, and no volume forecast, cost estimate, or spend cap is stated for the 48-worker fleet.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: send volume forecast and SES cost estimate

attacks.claim: Access controls for write and read on send_failures, which holds subscriber IDs, and SES credential scope are not described.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: IAM scope for send-worker and access controls on send_failures

attacks.claim: Sending depends on one provider in one region with no documented fallback or exit path.
attacks.evidence: "SES_REGION=us-east-1" and "calls SES SendBulkEmail"

attacks.claim: No accessibility review is listed for the Settings → Delivery toggle, the 'Not delivered' report, or the launch copy.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: accessibility review of Settings → Delivery and issue report

attacks.claim: The idle Sidekiq sender has no stated removal owner or date beyond the 14-day window, creating a dual code path.
attacks.evidence: "keep the Sidekiq sender deployed but idle for 14 days"
